source: CARDI (2011), "Handbook of Integrated Techniques for Increasing Wet-Season and Dry-Season Rice Productivity" (Khmer, 50pp, funded by CAVAC/ACIAR, foreword by H.E. Chan Sarun, Minister of Agriculture, dated 26 August 2011)
text: Background context on Cambodia's rice sector and CARDI's research impact, as presented in this 2011 handbook. Agriculture contributed about 29-30% of Cambodia's GDP around 2010, and about 80% of the population depends on farming for a livelihood; rice alone covers roughly 75% of all cultivated agricultural land. National rice production reached self-sufficiency in 1995 (ending a roughly 15-year deficit averaging about 500,000 tonnes/year since the fall of the Khmer Rouge regime) and grew to a surplus of about 3.7 million tonnes by 2010, on the back of yield growing from about 1.65 t/ha (1995) to 2.92 t/ha (2010); annual yield growth averaged about 4% overall (4.9%/year wet season, 3.3%/year dry season) alongside roughly 2.3%/year growth in cultivated area, and the surplus accelerated especially from 2005 to 2010 with a 2010 national surplus estimated at about 4 million tonnes of paddy. This is the production and self-sufficiency context behind the Cambodian government's 17 August 2010 policy promoting rice-milling/export and the national goal of exporting 1 million tonnes of milled rice by 2015. Between 1990 and 2010, CARDI released 38 new rice varieties to farmers, all still maintained for seed purity by CARDI's own annual seed-multiplication program. A survey across 14 provinces found the share of farmers growing a CARDI-released variety rose from about 17% (2003) to about 59% (2008); by 2008 this adoption was estimated to be worth roughly an extra 0.47 million tonnes of paddy production and over US$89 million in additional gross farmer income, nationally. On-farm yield-performance trials (percent yield advantage, %YA, over farmers' own varieties) for a sample of the 38 released varieties ranged from small or even negative in a few early-maturing lines up to roughly +20-27% for some medium/late-maturing and deepwater lines (for example Riang Chey at +26.0% wet season, CAR4 at +19.8%, Don at +24.8% for deepwater rice), illustrating that variety-replacement gains vary considerably by variety and by wet/dry season.
caveat: This is national background/statistical and institutional-history content rather than farmer-actionable technique, similar in kind to the history/institutional content this project has previously shoehorned into lifecycle_stage='plan' for lack of a better schema value (see the standing open item on whether a 'context'/'history' lifecycle_stage or separate category should be added to the schema). Figures are a 2010/2011 snapshot (self-sufficiency history, adoption rates, and yield-advantage trial results) and should not be read as current; likely overlaps with rice production/self-sufficiency history content already documented in this project from the separate CARDI 2007 book batches and should be duplicate-checked before merging.
